title: Oct 7 Results + Oct 8 Preview: When the Favorites Don't Show Up
summary: A tough 1-3 day on Oct 7, but here's what we're watching for tomorrow's slate.

content.value:
## Here's the Thing About October Baseball

Sometimes you walk into a day thinking the favorites have it locked, and then baseball reminds you why we love this game—nothing's guaranteed. October 7 was one of those humbling days where we went 1-3, hitting on just 25% of our picks. The Dodgers showed up for us, but the Sox, Yankees, and Padres? Not so much.

## How the Day Unfolded

Let's be honest—this one stung a little. We had four picks with relatively modest confidence levels, all hovering around 50-54%. The Dodgers pulled through at 51%, giving us our lone win. But the White Sox, Yankees, and Padres all fell short despite being our model's favorites. Days like this remind us that tight margins can swing either way, and today they swung against us.

## The Silver Lining

Here's what I keep coming back to: our confidence levels were honest. None of these were slam-dunks, and the model knew it. When you're picking games in the 50-54% range, you're essentially saying these could go either way. That's exactly what happened—just not in our favor. The key is learning and adjusting, not overreacting to one tough day.

## Looking Ahead to October 8

Tomorrow brings us a familiar matchup: Guardians at White Sox, round two. After missing on the White Sox yesterday at 50%, we're back on them again—same confidence level, new day. Parker Messick takes the mound for Cleveland against Chicago's Hagen Smith.

The model sees this as another coin-flip scenario, but there's something about the White Sox at home that keeps drawing our attention. Will tomorrow be redemption day, or will the Guardians prove us wrong twice in a row?

## The Bottom Line

A 1-3 day hurts, no question. But this is the marathon of baseball season, not a sprint. We trust the process, learn from the misses, and show up tomorrow ready to find the edge again. The White Sox get another chance to prove themselves, and so do we.

See you tomorrow for what we hope is a bounce-back day. Because here's the thing about baseball—there's always another game.
